**David Koepp** (;[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-1) born June 9, 1963) is an American screenwriter and director. As of February 2026, he is the fourth most successful screenwriter of all time in terms of U.S. box office receipts with a total gross of over $2.97 billion.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-2)

Koepp is known for a variety of screenplays, including those of the [Steven Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg")–directed films _[Jurassic Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_Park "Jurassic Park")_ (1993), _[The Lost World: Jurassic Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lost\_World:\_Jurassic\_Park "The Lost World: Jurassic Park")_ (1997), _[War of the Worlds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War\_of\_the\_Worlds\_(2005\_film) "War of the Worlds (2005 film)")_ (2005), _[Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana\_Jones\_and\_the\_Kingdom\_of\_the\_Crystal\_Skull "Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull")_ (2008) and _[Disclosure Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disclosure\_Day "Disclosure Day")_ (2026). Other Koepp screenplays include those for the crime film _[Carlito's Way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlito's\_Way "Carlito's Way")_ (1993); the action spy films _[Mission: Impossible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission:\_Impossible\_(film) "Mission: Impossible (film)")_ (1996) and _[Jack Ryan: Shadow Recruit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack\_Ryan:\_Shadow\_Recruit "Jack Ryan: Shadow Recruit")_ (2014); the superhero film _[Spider-Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man\_(2002\_film) "Spider-Man (2002 film)")_ (2002); another _[Indiana Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana\_Jones "Indiana Jones")_ film, _[The Dial of Destiny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana\_Jones\_and\_the\_Dial\_of\_Destiny "Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny")_ (2023); and another _[Jurassic Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_Park\_(franchise) "Jurassic Park (franchise)")_ film, _[Jurassic World Rebirth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_World\_Rebirth "Jurassic World Rebirth")_ (2025).

Koepp has also directed seven feature films: _[The Trigger Effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Trigger\_Effect "The Trigger Effect")_ (1996), _[Stir of Echoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stir\_of\_Echoes "Stir of Echoes")_ (1999), _[Secret Window](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret\_Window "Secret Window")_ (2004), _[Ghost Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost\_Town\_(2008\_film) "Ghost Town (2008 film)")_ (2008), _[Premium Rush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premium\_Rush "Premium Rush")_ (2012), _[Mortdecai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mortdecai\_(film) "Mortdecai (film)")_ (2015), and _[You Should Have Left](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You\_Should\_Have\_Left "You Should Have Left")_ (2020).

Koepp was born in [Pewaukee, Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pewaukee,_Wisconsin "Pewaukee, Wisconsin"), as the youngest of four children to Margaret (Fairfield), a family therapist, and Donald Koepp, who owned a [billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_(advertising) "Billboard (advertising)") company.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-LATimes1994-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-6)

Originally studying to become an actor, first at the [University of Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Minnesota "University of Minnesota") for one year and afterwards at the [University of Wisconsin–Madison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Wisconsin%E2%80%93Madison "University of Wisconsin–Madison") for two years, he enrolled in the film school of the [University of California, Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Los_Angeles "University of California, Los Angeles"), in 1984.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-LATimes1994-3)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-8) He graduated with a bachelor's degree in film from UCLA in 1990.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-9)

As a writer, Koepp worked on blockbuster [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_(film_industry) "Hollywood (film industry)") films such as _[Jurassic Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_Park\_(film) "Jurassic Park (film)")_ with [Steven Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg"), _[Mission: Impossible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission:\_Impossible\_(film) "Mission: Impossible (film)")_ with [Brian De Palma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_De_Palma "Brian De Palma") and _[Spider-Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man\_(2002\_film) "Spider-Man (2002 film)")_ with [Sam Raimi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi "Sam Raimi").

Koepp had a [cameo appearance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameo_appearance "Cameo appearance") as the "Unlucky Bastard", a minor character devoured by a _[T. rex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrannosaurus "Tyrannosaurus")_ that roams [San Diego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego "San Diego") in _[The Lost World: Jurassic Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lost\_World:\_Jurassic\_Park "The Lost World: Jurassic Park")_, which he co-wrote and for which he was a second unit director. Although Koepp did not write _[Jurassic Park III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_Park\_III "Jurassic Park III")_, he did devise the film's basic storyline.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-11) Koepp later declined an offer to write a script for the fourth film in the series, _[Jurassic World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_World "Jurassic World")_, as he felt he had nothing left to contribute to the series.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-12)

Koepp was reportedly paid $4,000,000 for his _[Panic Room](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panic\_Room\_(film) "Panic Room (film)")_ screenplay. He wrote the screenplay for _[Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana\_Jones\_and\_the\_Kingdom\_of\_the\_Crystal\_Skull "Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull")_ for [Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg") and [George Lucas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Lucas "George Lucas") and co-wrote and directed 2008's _[Ghost Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost\_Town\_(2008\_film) "Ghost Town (2008 film)")_ starring [Ricky Gervais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Gervais "Ricky Gervais") and [Greg Kinnear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Kinnear "Greg Kinnear").

Koepp's work as a director has not had quite the same box office success. His films include _[Secret Window](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret\_Window "Secret Window")_, _[Stir of Echoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stir\_of\_Echoes "Stir of Echoes")_, and _[The Trigger Effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Trigger\_Effect "The Trigger Effect")_. Koepp has worked in television, creating the 2002 series _[Hack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hack\_(TV\_series) "Hack (TV series)")_ starring [David Morse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Morse_(actor) "David Morse (actor)").

In 2012, Koepp directed _[Premium Rush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premium\_Rush "Premium Rush")_, which he co-wrote with John Kamps.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-13) In an August 2011 lawsuit, [Joe Quirk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Quirk "Joe Quirk"), the author of the 1998 novel _[The Ultimate Rush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ultimate\_Rush "The Ultimate Rush")_, accused Koepp and the makers of _Premium Rush_ of copyright infringement.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-14) On April 2, 2013, [U.S. District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_District?action=edit&redlink=1 "United States District (page does not exist)") Judge [Richard Seeborg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Seeborg "Richard Seeborg") dismissed this case, finding that the two works were not substantially similar.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-15)

On February 17, 2013, Koepp received the WGA East's Ian McClellan Hunter Award for Career Achievement.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-16)

On July 10, 2013, [Lionsgate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionsgate_Films "Lionsgate Films") was reported to have acquired the comedic crime novel _The Great Mortdecai Moustache Mystery_, written by [Kyril Bonfiglioli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyril_Bonfiglioli "Kyril Bonfiglioli").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-17) Koepp directed the film, titled _[Mortdecai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mortdecai\_(film) "Mortdecai (film)")_, from a script by Eric Aronson.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-18)[Johnny Depp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Depp "Johnny Depp") played the lead role of Charlie Mortdecai,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-19) and the film also featured [Gwyneth Paltrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwyneth_Paltrow "Gwyneth Paltrow"), [Ewan McGregor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ewan_McGregor "Ewan McGregor"), and [Paul Bettany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Bettany "Paul Bettany").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-20) Koepp adapted the [Marcus Sakey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcus_Sakey "Marcus Sakey") novel _Brilliance_, which will star [Will Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Smith "Will Smith") and [Noomi Rapace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noomi_Rapace "Noomi Rapace").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-21)

On March 15, 2016, [The Walt Disney Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company "The Walt Disney Company") announced [a fifth installment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana_Jones_and_the_Dial_of_Destiny "Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny") of the _[Indiana Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana\_Jones "Indiana Jones")_ saga, with Koepp as its screenwriter and [Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg") directing again.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-23) By June 2018, Koepp ultimately backed out of the project due to his commitment to _[You Should Have Left](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You\_Should\_Have\_Left "You Should Have Left")_, a horror drama film Koepp wrote and directed.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-24) Based on the novel of the same name by [Daniel Kehlmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Kehlmann "Daniel Kehlmann"), _You Should Have Left_ was released in 2020, and stars [Kevin Bacon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Bacon "Kevin Bacon") and [Amanda Seyfried](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanda_Seyfried "Amanda Seyfried").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-26)

On September 3, 2019, Koepp made his novel debut with the publication of _Cold Storage_, a science-fiction thriller.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-27) A [film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_Storage_(film) "Cold Storage (film)") was announced in May 2022 from [Studiocanal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studiocanal "Studiocanal"), with Koepp writing the screenplay and [Jonny Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonny_Campbell "Jonny Campbell") directing; the cast consists of [Liam Neeson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liam_Neeson "Liam Neeson"), [Joe Keery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Keery "Joe Keery"), [Georgina Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgina_Campbell "Georgina Campbell"), and [Sosie Bacon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sosie_Bacon "Sosie Bacon").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-29)

On December 10, 2020, [Amasia Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amasia_Entertainment "Amasia Entertainment") and [Universal Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Pictures "Universal Pictures") announced Koepp had been tapped to write the script for a reboot of the [Green Hornet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Hornet "Green Hornet") franchise titled _The Green Hornet and Kato_.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-30) On February 25, 2021, it was announced Koepp would write and co-produce the thriller _[Kimi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kimi\_(film) "Kimi (film)")_, directed by [Steven Soderbergh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Soderbergh "Steven Soderbergh") and starring [Zoë Kravitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zo%C3%AB_Kravitz "Zoë Kravitz").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-31) The film was released on [Max](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_(streaming_service) "Max (streaming service)") (then HBO Max) on February 10, 2022.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-32)

Koepp's second novel _Aurora_ was published on June 7, 2022, and a film adaptation of the book is in development for [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix"), with Koepp writing the script and [Kathryn Bigelow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathryn_Bigelow "Kathryn Bigelow") directing.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-33)

Koepp wrote the screenplay for the psychological thriller film _[Presence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presence\_(2024\_film) "Presence (2024 film)")_, which was directed by Soderbergh and premiered at the [2024 Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Sundance_Film_Festival "2024 Sundance Film Festival").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-34) Koepp would reunite with Soderbergh on spy film _[Black Bag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black\_Bag "Black Bag")_, which was released in theatres on March 14, 2025 by [Focus Features](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Focus_Features "Focus Features").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-36) On January 22, 2024, it was announced that Koepp would return to the _[Jurassic Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_Park\_(franchise) "Jurassic Park (franchise)")_ franchise by writing _[Jurassic World Rebirth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_World\_Rebirth "Jurassic World Rebirth")_, with [Gareth Edwards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gareth_Edwards_(filmmaker) "Gareth Edwards (filmmaker)") directing and Spielberg serving as executive producer.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-38) In April 2024, it was confirmed that Koepp and Spielberg would work again on an original film about [UFOs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unidentified_flying_object "Unidentified flying object"),[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-40) later revealed to be titled _[Disclosure Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disclosure\_Day "Disclosure Day")_ with a planned June 2026 release.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-41)

Koepp was married to artist Rosario Varela, with whom he has two children.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-LATimes1994-3)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-42) After they divorced, Koepp married writer Melissa Thomas, with whom he also has two children.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-44)
